tables.name: services
tables.description: The business's services, one row per line of its list (S1-12 gives services): the name, the price kind, the time it takes, the order, whether it is offered, and what the profession file says about it. The kind of work each line was matched to is named. Where a service happens and how it is paid there are service_money's rows; every price is a price rule (price_rules), since every price carries effective dates (arch 09 line 488). A service is never deleted or re-keyed: one no longer offered is set inactive, so its id stays stable for K-26's rules for some services (QUESTIONS.md CQ-51), K-30's booking lines and K-32's packs and memberships.
tables.source: 02-contracts section 7 row K-25 ('Services (name, price kind, price, length, places, order, active, extras)'); FS line 724 (service); FS rows V01 to V04; S1-12 (gives services); arch 09 line 457 ('Service: length · price kind'); 02-contracts section 8 (services: K-25 service rows); QUESTIONS.md CQ-51

tables.name: service_money
tables.description: Where each service happens and how it is paid there (FS service_money; S1-13 gives ways): one row per service and place, since 'a service in two places has two prices and two money rows'. Each row holds the place (L01, as S1-43 allows), its flow, its money path (one of the master's 28 for that flow), the deposit and the late-cancel and no-show fee, and this way's own free-cancel time and tip line where the owner set one (else the business's: K-23 flow_defaults, K-26's tip_line rule). The price is a price rule (price_rules), whose place condition names this row; the rest and the amount paid in full are worked out by code, never stored. A change applies to new bookings at once: each booking copies its way in (K-30, written once).
tables.source: 02-contracts section 7 row K-25 ('service money per flow, place and path with its amounts, cutoff and tips (FS service and service_money rows)'); FS line 725 (service_money); FS rows L01, V05 to V08, V11; FS section 4; S1-13 (gives ways); S1-43; S11-56; 02-contracts section 8 (ways: K-25 service money per path)

tables.name: price_rules
tables.description: Every price (arch 09 line 457: 'Price rule: worker · place · time'): one row per price of a service, with the conditions it holds under (the place, the worker, the time; none set: the service's own price) and effective dates (arch 09 line 488). The rule with the most conditions set wins; a possible tie, two rules with as many conditions that can both apply, is caught when the owner saves the second, and the read-back asks which wins (price_rule_ties); until answered, the lower price applies (arch 05 line 253; S13-25 rule 19). A change closes one row and opens the next: a rule prices visits that start inside its dates, read when the booking is made, and the booking line copies the winner (K-30), so a booking keeps the price it was made with. Code fills every price from the owner's words read back; the model never writes one (BP rule 4).

checks.source: FS row T06 (price by person); K-04 v1 resources_kind_known

checks.name: price_rules_weekdays_form
checks.expression: weekdays is null or (weekdays ~ '^1?2?3?4?5?6?7?$' and length(weekdays) between 1 and 6)
checks.source: arch 05 line 253 (time); one form per condition, so price_rules_one_in_effect compares like with like (every day is no day condition)

checks.name: price_rules_times_form
checks.expression: (from_time is null or from_time > time '00:00') and (until_time is null or until_time < time '24:00') and (from_time is null or until_time is null or from_time < until_time)
checks.source: arch 05 line 253 (time); one form per condition (a day's start or end is no clock condition)

checks.name: price_rules_money
checks.expression: price_cents >= 0 and (from_cents is null or from_cents > 0) and currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'
checks.source: FS rows V02 ('free = a list price of $0'), V03; CQ-09

checks.name: price_rules_dates_in_order
checks.expression: effective_to is null or effective_to > effective_from
checks.source: arch 09 line 488

indexes.name: price_rules_service_idx
indexes.why: A service's rules in effect at a visit's start: the price resolver (arch 05 line 253; C-131), search's five rows with exact prices (arch 05 line 239), the times card (A4-14) and the read-back at a save (S11-54).

tables.name: price_rule_ties
tables.description: A possible tie between two price rules of one service (arch 05 line 253): rules with as many conditions set that can both apply to one booking, caught when the owner saves the second. The read-back asks which wins; the owner's answer is kept here. Until it is answered, the lower price applies (S13-25 rule 19). One row per pair caught.
tables.source: arch 05 line 253 ('A possible tie is caught when the owner saves the second rule: the read-back asks which wins (DD). Until answered, the lower price applies (S13-25 rule 19)'); 02-contracts section 7 row K-25 ('a possible tie is caught at the second save'); S13-25 rule 19 ('The safer one wins until settled: ... less money')

columns.name: id
columns.description: The tie's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The service's business, held to it by price_rule_ties_service_fk, so row-level security can scope the row.
columns.source: arch 10 line 546

columns.name: service_id
columns.description: The service both rules price (services.id).
columns.source: arch 05 line 253

columns.name: first_rule_id
columns.description: The rule saved first (price_rules.id).
columns.source: arch 05 line 253 ('when the owner saves the second rule')

columns.name: second_rule_id
columns.description: The rule whose save caught the tie (price_rules.id).
columns.source: arch 05 line 253

columns.name: asked_at
columns.description: When the read-back of the second save asked which wins.
columns.source: arch 05 line 253 ('the read-back asks which wins')

columns.name: winner_rule_id
columns.description: The rule the owner said wins where both apply: first_rule_id or second_rule_id. Null until answered, and meanwhile the lower price applies.
columns.source: arch 05 line 253 ('Until answered, the lower price applies'); S13-25 rule 19

columns.name: answered_at
columns.description: When the owner answered; null until then.
columns.source: arch 05 line 253

columns.name: answered_by_person_id
columns.description: Who answered (persons.id): the owner, or an admin the owner lets set prices; null until answered.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

unique.name: price_rule_ties_pair_key
unique.source: arch 05 line 253 (one question per tie caught)

checks.name: price_rule_ties_two_rules
checks.expression: first_rule_id <> second_rule_id
checks.source: arch 05 line 253 ('the second rule')

checks.name: price_rule_ties_winner_of_pair
checks.expression: winner_rule_id is null or winner_rule_id in (first_rule_id, second_rule_id)
checks.source: arch 05 line 253 ('the read-back asks which wins')

checks.name: price_rule_ties_answer_together
checks.expression: (winner_rule_id is null) = (answered_at is null) and (answered_at is null) = (answered_by_person_id is null) and (answered_at is null or answered_at >= asked_at)
checks.source: arch 05 line 253 ('Until answered')

indexes.name: price_rule_ties_service_idx
indexes.why: A service's ties and their answers, read with its rules by the price resolver (arch 05 line 253).
